$comment: The Merlin Agent Windows collection manifest.
THIS FILE IS THE COMPLETE LIST OF WHAT THE AGENT READS. Every query below runs through
osqueryi and nothing else is collected. An administrator can paste any of them into
osqueryi on their own machine and get byte-identical output — which is a far stronger
assurance than reading the agent's source, and is the main reason collection is delegated
to osquery rather than hand-rolled.
NOTHING HERE READS WHO IS SIGNED IN. There is no query for the interactive user, the
session, the console owner or any mail address. The entra_join query is the one place a
user field is even nearby, and it names the two values it wants so the rest cannot be
returned — see its own comment.
A query that fails or returns nothing produces a NULL reading, never a false one. Merlin
treats null as 'not observed' and will not raise a nonconformity from it.
QUERIES RUN IN THE ORDER LISTED HERE, AND THE ORDER IS DELIBERATE. A collection is bounded so
it cannot hold the machine lock past the point where the updater gives up waiting for it, and
on a machine where osquery answers slowly that bound is reached before the end of this list.
Whatever is left is reported as NOT OBSERVED, so the security-posture queries come first and
the inventory ones last: losing a hostname degrades a device page, while losing disk encryption
or the firewall loses the reading the ISMS exists to take.

bitlocker.sql: SELECT drive_letter, protection_status, conversion_status, encryption_method, percentage_encrypted FROM bitlocker_info;
bitlocker.purpose: Per-volume disk encryption state, including Windows Home Device Encryption.

os_edition.sql: SELECT data FROM registry WHERE path = 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\EditionID';
os_edition.purpose: Edition (Home / Pro / Server). Gates which controls can physically apply — a Home machine cannot run BitLocker, so an unprotected volume there is a licensing fact rather than a protection somebody switched off. It runs directly after `bitlocker` because it is what decides how those rows are graded.

security_products.sql: SELECT name, state, state_timestamp FROM windows_security_products WHERE type = 'Antivirus';
security_products.purpose: The registered antimalware product and whether the platform considers it healthy.

security_center.sql: SELECT antivirus, firewall, autoupdate FROM windows_security_center;
security_center.purpose: The platform's own summary of antivirus, firewall and update health.

firewall_profiles.sql: SELECT path, data FROM registry WHERE path LIKE 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\SharedAccess\Parameters\FirewallPolicy\%Profile\EnableFirewall';
firewall_profiles.purpose: Whether each firewall profile (domain, private, public) is enabled.

tpm.sql: SELECT activated, enabled, spec_version FROM tpm_info;
tpm.purpose: Whether a TPM is present and usable — the precondition for a non-exportable signing key.

inactivity_timeout.sql: SELECT data FROM registry WHERE path = 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\InactivityTimeoutSecs';
inactivity_timeout.purpose: The machine-wide inactivity lock timeout (A.7.7 clear screen).

patches.sql: SELECT hotfix_id, installed_on FROM patches ORDER BY installed_on DESC LIMIT 5;
patches.purpose: When an update was last installed. A count of PENDING updates is not collected in v1 — see docs/collection-manifest.md.

os_version.sql: SELECT name, version, build, platform FROM os_version;
os_version.purpose: Operating system name, version and build — what end-of-support is judged against.

$comment: Returns LOCAL ACCOUNT names, not the identity of whoever is signed in. A.8.2 is
materially weaker without them: a count says there are four local administrators but
not that one of them is unexpected. Flagged here rather than buried.
local_admins.sql: SELECT u.username FROM users u JOIN user_groups ug ON u.uid = ug.uid JOIN groups g ON ug.gid = g.gid WHERE g.groupname = 'Administrators';

$comment: ONE COLUMN, NAMED. `security_profile_info` also carries the local Administrator and
Guest account names and nine audit-policy settings; none of that is wanted, so the
query names the single column it needs and the rest cannot be returned — the same
rule the entra_join query follows.
This does NOT run secedit and writes nothing to disk. osquery calls
SceGetSecurityProfileInfo in scecli.dll in process and frees the result; the temporary
file that the secedit CLI would leave behind is the reason this was left uncollected
until now, and it does not exist on this path.
-1 MEANS NOT CONFIGURED, NOT 'OFF'. osquery clamps the SCE no-value sentinel to -1, so
only 0 and 1 are answers. Reading -1 as false would fail every machine whose policy SCE
could not read, against a value nobody measured.
The table also exposes password length, both ages, history and the lockout threshold.
Those are deliberately NOT taken from here: its maximum_password_age of -1 cannot be
told apart from 'not configured', where `net accounts` prints the word 'Unlimited'.
One value, one source.
password_complexity.purpose: Whether local passwords must meet complexity requirements (A.5.17).

system_drive.sql: SELECT device_id, free_space, size FROM logical_drives WHERE type = 'Fixed' AND device_id = 'C:';
system_drive.purpose: Free space on the system volume (A.8.6 capacity).

system_info.sql: SELECT hostname, hardware_serial, hardware_vendor, hardware_model FROM system_info;
system_info.purpose: Machine identity, and the serial used to reconcile against the asset register.

machine_guid.sql: SELECT data FROM registry WHERE path = 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Cryptography\MachineGuid';
machine_guid.purpose: Stable machine identifier that survives a rename.

chassis.purpose: Laptop / desktop / server, used to pre-fill an asset record.

$comment: THE PRIVACY-CRITICAL QUERY. The CloudDomainJoin key also contains user-identifying
values on some machines. This query names exactly the two it wants in its WHERE clause,
so the others are never returned to the agent at all — the restriction is enforced by
the query rather than by the agent remembering to ignore them.
entra_join.sql: SELECT name, data FROM registry WHERE key LIKE 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\CloudDomainJoin\JoinInfo\%' AND name IN ('DeviceId', 'TenantId');
entra_join.purpose: The machine's Entra device id — the exact join key for fleet coverage. Absent on a workgroup machine, which is a true fact about the machine.
